item.content:encoded: Basically this. People being added to the group, this I understood. But there being no mechanism in the article for the reduction of people in the group means that adding new members to it is NOT containment, it is allowing the scp to continue to operate. If it fully consumed one member a month then feeding it a new member to keep its mass stable would make sense. But aiding its growth and thus presumably its intelligence on a MONTHLY BASIS is a TERRIBLE idea, and the scientist responsible for making that the procedure needs to be transferred and reviewed.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Yes, but if the thing is just locked in a vault that cannot be opened from the inside, as in no interior mechanisms that can be tampered with or locks to pick or gullible scientists to hear sobbing, then unless it can walk through walls or damage the containment with just the muscle-power of the enslaved bodies then who cares how angry or hungry it gets? I say put it in an enclosure with steel walls a foot thick and just weld the door shut. Slap some sound-proofing on it and never worry about it again. I really cannot image why feeding it would be an option when doing so can only make it more dangerous and difficult to contain over time.

I can see what you're thinking, but the author built the reasoning for that procedure into the description pretty well: if it does not get a new human member, it is markedly more dangerous in its active/hunting state. The example of a containment breach is provided to make this even clearer. It isn't "do what they say" cliche because the thing is difficult to physically damage— so it sort of ends the article with a catch-22. Which is worse, dealing with it when it's hungry, or making it docile but bigger?

+1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I find fault with this in the containment procedure:

A single D-Class personnel due for termination is to be offered once per month to keep SCP-428 satisfied, however this will result in the need for an increase in containment space or for a solution to keep SCP-428 neutralised in the future.

In what universe would making an SCP bigger and more dangerous be the best option for containment? Who cares how "satisfied" it is! Beyond knowing what it's components knew, what would be the risk of simply containing it like any other dangerous SCP animal? If it were sealed in a vault then even if all the smartest people in the world were added to it, they couldn't muscle their way out with their bare hands.

Giving it more D-classes would qualify it for these SCP cliches:
3. Things what we should do what they say becuz we wouldn't like them when they're angry.
7. Things what use up excessive resources, like nucular weaponz or Class-D personnel.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Okay, I cleaned it up a bit but did no actual editing, so a few things still feel off, mostly because I have no idea what you were getting at. In particular, this sentence,

Wounds inflicted upon SCP-428’s crowd heal at an accelerated rate, do not hinder movement and been proven to be highly resilient.

makes no sense, particularly the last two phrases. It's said again later that wounds to the legs do not hinder movement, so you don't need that, while "[have] been proven to be highly resilient" is said of the members of the crowd, not the wounds inflicted thereupon. I take it the meaning is that it's hard to really damage them. You could probably achieve the same effect phrased something like "Members of SCP-428's crowd have proven to be highly resilient, as inflicted wounds heal at an accelerated rate."

I also think you could expand a bit on what happens when crowd members are separated from the central mass. The fluid leaks out, repairing the hole, I take it, but then what happens to the remains? I assume the person dies.

That said, I'll upvote this now, because I still so love the concept.
